text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Seven soldiers wounded in Lebanon. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu: Talk of Lebanon pullout encourages Hizbollah.
- Netanyahu and Palestinian President Arafat agree to resume negotiations on Sunday on their interim peace deal.
- Two hundred Sikorsky helicopters grounded recently by U.S. Marines and Navy for six months due to production defect.
- About 20 million shekels ($6 million) that Education Ministry was to have transferred to immigrants, never reached them.
- Israel's insurance against coastal pollution damage to expire in 10 days.
- Israeli procurers bringing non-Jewish minor girls from former Soviet Union to Israel, to employ them as prostitutes.
JERUSALEM POST
- Security talks with Palestinians start Sunday.
- Hizbollah wounds seven Israeli soldiers in Lebanon zone.
- French envoy links Israeli withdrawal to Golan deal.
- European Union wrote letter of Hebron assurance to Arafat.
- Antwerp Jews bid to recover Nazi-looted diamonds.
MAARIV
- Discussions in army on operational changes in Lebanon.
- "Positive meeting" between Netanyahu and Arafat.
- Highest wage-earner in Israel's public sector suspected of income tax evasion.
- Police investigating suspicion of fraud in attorney-general appointment affair.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai oppose changes in Israel's military deployment in Lebanon.
- Police investigating suspicion that ex-minister blackmailed officials in prime minister's office.
- Arafat asked Netanyahu to free additional Palestinian prisoners.
GLOBES
- Claridge group returns to vie for Bank Hapoalim.
- Government cannot make structural changes in Bank Hapoalim without legislation.
